title: Warehouse registry
subDomain: one shared list of bin locations

act2.summary: a second fulfilment site needs its own bin registry, live in the same process as the first - exactly the guarantee a single shared instance is built to prevent

solutions.title: A class with a private constructor and getInstance()
solutions.tradeoff: Cheaper than the no-pattern baseline and the module route, because there's a class to reuse: createWarehouseRegistry() calls a new static method that constructs a second instance from inside the class itself, bypassing getInstance() without relaxing the private constructor. Still costs more than injection - three methods have to be wrapped in a plain object to match the shared handle shape, and a clear() method has to be added to the class first.

solutions.title: Module-level state, no class at all
solutions.tradeoff: As expensive as the no-pattern baseline, for the same reason: no reusable unit to instantiate a second time, so createWarehouseRegistry() has to hand-duplicate registerBin/binLocation/binsInAisle/clear's logic into a closure from scratch. A module has exactly one instance per process - the same guarantee a singleton class makes, without a class to fall back on when that guarantee is exactly what act 2 needs undone.

solutions.title: An explicit createWarehouseRegistry() factory, no shared instance
solutions.tradeoff: Already built for this: createWarehouseRegistry() has existed since act 1, because this route was never built around one shared instance. Act 2 costs one export line - the factory just wasn't part of the frozen act-1 boundary yet.

reviewFocus: Does the chosen candidate's WALKTHROUGH.md name what would change my mind about the choice, or does it just describe the code?
Is 'a second live instance is exactly the guarantee a singleton is built to prevent' a fair reading of why Singleton and a module both measure worse here?
In the singleton route, does createWarehouseRegistry() really produce an instance independent of getInstance()'s cached one, with no shared state leaking between them?
Do all four routes - and the no-pattern baseline - agree, byte for byte, on registerBin/binLocation/binsInAisle/resetRegistry for act 1, before any of them has two registries at once?
Would a reader's CHOICE.md, written before act 2, have predicted that 'exactly one instance' is the one guarantee three of these four routes can't cheaply undo?
